n: A new series of ten promises begins, each opening “Thus saith the Lord of hosts.”

f.w: the word of the LORD of hosts
f.g: Zechariah 8 contains ten short oracles of hope.

n: God is fiercely devoted to Zion, burning with zeal to protect her.
The Lord has returned and will live in Jerusalem. It will be called the City of Truth (Faithfulness), and His mountain the Holy Mountain.
Elderly men and women will again sit in Jerusalem’s streets, leaning on canes — a sign of long, peaceful lives.
The streets will be full of boys and girls playing. Few images of peace are more beautiful than safe, happy children.
This may seem too wonderful to the struggling remnant, but is it too hard for God? Nothing is impossible with Him.

f.w: should it also be marvellous in mine eyes?

n: God will rescue His people from east and west — from everywhere.

f.w: from the east country, and from the west country

n: They will live in Jerusalem and be His people, and He will be their God in faithfulness and righteousness — the heart of the covenant.

f.w: they shall be my people, and I will be their God

n: Let your hands be strong, you who heard the prophets when the temple foundation was laid. Keep building!
Before the work began, there were no wages, no profit for man or beast, and no safety — everyone was against everyone.

f.w: there was no hire for man

n: But now God will treat this remnant differently than before.
Seed will prosper, vines bear fruit, the ground yield crops, and the sky give dew. God will give all this to the remnant.

f.w: the heavens shall give their dew

n: Judah and Israel had been a byword for a curse among nations; now God will save them, and they will be a blessing. Don’t fear — be strong.
Just as God determined to punish their ancestors and did not relent…

f.g: I did not relent or change My mind.

n: …so now He is determined to do good to Jerusalem and Judah. Don’t be afraid. God’s determination to bless is as firm as His justice.
Here is what you must do: speak truth to one another and give true, peaceful verdicts in your courts.

f.w: Speak ye every man the truth to his neighbour

f.g: The city gates, where courts met.

n: Don’t plot evil against your neighbor, and don’t love false oaths — God hates these things.

f.w: all these are things that I hate

n: Another word from the Lord — now He finally answers the question about fasting from chapter 7.

f.w: the word of the LORD of hosts came unto me

n: The four fasts mourning Jerusalem’s fall will become joyful feasts. Sorrow will turn to gladness. So love truth and peace.

f.w: The fast of the fourth month

n: People from many cities will come.
People from one city will urge others: “Let’s go at once to pray to the Lord! I’m going too.” Faith spreads by invitation.
Many peoples and powerful nations will come to Jerusalem to seek and pray to the Lord.

f.w: many people and strong nations shall come

n: Ten people from every language will grab the robe of one Jew and say, “Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.” Israel will become a light drawing the world to God.

f.g: The hem or fringe (tassel) of the robe, a sign of covenant (Numbers 15:38-39).
